decisions.rationale: Claim verified true; consolidated with sme-fcc-v1. Reproduced by the reconciler on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 044631bf with the private overlay copied over the starter, using the overlay's own reference learner test unless stated otherwise. The reconciler changed only the solved form's submit button content by adding a decorative aria-hidden prefix before the label, which leaves the accessible name 'Save service'. The normal run shows 'Test Files 8 passed (8)' and 'Tests 8 passed (8)', then npm test exits 1 with the blank-ignored, blank-saves and complete-ignored misses, each asking for an assertion the test already makes. Cause, confirmed from the code: isThisForm (lines 25-29) compares each button's trimmed textContent with submitLabel and, on a mismatch, the listener returns without injecting the fault and without writing the unreadable mark, so the run neither applies the fault nor fails closed. The verdict errs only toward rejection: a weak test cannot use this path to be accepted. Severity: low, agreed. A correct learner does not reach this through the shipped workflow. The starter ships a plain submit button whose only content is submitLabel, the starter test passes submitLabel 'Save service', and README tasks 1-8 never ask for icons, decorative content, aria-label or input type=submit on the button. The reconciler also checked the pending-label pattern that tests 3 and 4 accept ('Saving' while onSave is pending): the solved form uses it and is accepted, because the capture listener runs before React re-renders, so the button text still equals submitLabel when each submit fires. Reaching v1 needs the learner to change shipped markup beyond what the README asks. Fix direction (one consolidated fix for edu-fcc-v1 and sme-fcc-v1, in tests/task8-variant.jsx only): stop matching the submit button's raw textContent. Treat the submitted form as this instance's when exactly one variant instance is mounted; otherwise match the submit control with Testing Library's button-role query by accessible name within the submitted form, as the public tests find it. Optionally, when the submitted form holds both labelled fields but fails the scope check, write the unreadable mark so the run fails closed. Add decorated-button, input-type-submit and defaulted-submitLabel forms to the private adversarial controls. Feasibility: the reconciler trialled this in scratch (mounted-instance count plus role query, combined with the sme-fcc-v2 label change). The decorated-button, input-type-submit and defaulted-label probes, the aria-labelledby caption outside the form and the inside caption were each accepted with the Task 8 line and exit 0. The unchanged solved form was still accepted. A blank-only test of the reconciler's own was still rejected with the four completed-submission messages, and a name-only objectContaining test with only the team message. The SME's two-form and StrictMode trials are critic-reported, not rerun. This finding does not justify a fifth loop on its own; include it only if Firstmate authorizes one. Correction-loop status: this lab has already had four correction loops (89064f80, 30cd7583, 8543f338 and 044631bf, the last authorized by Firstmate under key react-forms-loop4-correction). Any byte-changing fix for this finding is a fifth correction loop and needs a new Firstmate decision. The author must not edit any lab byte for it until Firstmate makes that decision. Firstmate's condition for a fifth loop (a substantive medium or high finding remains) is not met by this finding. Residual edu-fcc-u5 (solved run): the worker's re-record in the worktree, coding-lab-solved-run.json, records run solved-1795025657 at 044631bf. The reconciler checked that it binds all 37 files tracked under the lab at 044631bf by their current sha256, with no mismatch and no extra entry. It names the control and six variants, lists the private adversarial controls, and states that Windows and Linux were not run and are unverified. That answers the three gaps the education critic named, and the reconciler also reran the shipped starter at 044631bf (Test Files 8 failed (8), Tests 8 failed (8), exit 1, oracle not reached). The loop-4 accept decision on edu-fcc-u5 stands and needs no new decision. Formal closure still needs the change committed and an education recheck bound to the new solved-run bytes, because the loop-5 recheck item is open and bound to the old solved-run hash. If Firstmate authorizes a fifth loop, the solved run must be re-recorded again at that loop's commit.

Claim verified true; consolidated with sme-fcc-v2. Reproduced by the reconciler on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 044631bf with the private overlay copied over the starter, using the overlay's own reference learner test unless stated otherwise. The reconciler removed the solved form's name label, rendered a caption with the 'Service name' text just outside the form element in the same component, and pointed the name input at it with aria-labelledby. The normal run shows 'Tests 8 passed (8)', so test 2 has already found both labels, then npm test exits 1 with the single fail-closed message telling the learner to finish tasks 1-2 so every field has a label. Tasks 1-2 are done, so the advice is wrong. Fail-closed behaviour itself is correct: one message, exit 1 and no false misses. With the same caption inside the form, the run is accepted with the Task 8 line and exit 0. Severity: low, agreed. A correct learner does not reach this through the shipped workflow. README task 2 and the starter TASK 2 comment ask for htmlFor/id association with the label inside the existing field markup. Reaching the path needs the learner to replace that association with aria-labelledby and move the caption outside the form element. The impact is a misleading diagnosis on a run that correctly does not accept, not a wrong verdict. Fix direction (one consolidated fix for edu-fcc-v2 and sme-fcc-v2): in tests/task8-variant.jsx, run the label-text query from the document body, as test 2 does, and keep only a match inside the submitted form. In tests/verify-learner-test.mjs, reword the unreadable message so that it does not send the learner back to tasks 1-2. It should say that the Task 8 check could not read the 'Service name' and 'Owning team' fields of the form your test submitted, and that each field should be labelled inside the form element. Keep the fail-closed behaviour. Feasibility: the reconciler trialled the label-query change in scratch together with the v1 change, and the outside-caption form was accepted with exit 0 (see edu-fcc-v1). The message rewording was not trialled. Residual sme-fcc-u5 (deleted learner test file): this belongs with this fix because it is in the same verifier file. The loop-4 escalate decision on sme-fcc-u5 stands and needs no new decision. The loop-4 fix was incomplete on an item that the fourth loop authorized. Reproduced: with starter/src/service-form.test.jsx deleted, the normal run shows 'Test Files 7 passed (7)' and 'Tests 7 passed (7)', then the control message 'your test fails against an unchanged copy of your finished form', exit 1. The exit 1 verdict is correct and only the diagnosis is wrong. Cause: a control run with no test files exits non-zero, so control.clean is false and the no-runnable-test branch is skipped. Fix direction: choose the no-runnable message when the control run has no failed and no passed assertions, whatever its exit status. Trialled in scratch: the deleted-file case then prints 'no runnable test was found in starter/src/service-form.test.jsx ...', exit 1. The reference test was still accepted. This finding does not justify a fifth loop on its own; include it only if Firstmate authorizes one. Claim verified true; consolidated with edu-fcc-v2, which carries the reproduction, severity reasoning, fix direction and the sme-fcc-u5 residual. The cause given by the SME matches the code. fieldByLabel (line 14) queries within the submitted form, and Testing Library resolves an aria-labelledby id inside the query container, while test 2 queries from document.body through screen. So a caption outside the form satisfies test 2 but not the variant. The cited @testing-library/dom 10.4.2 label-helpers source is critic-reported and consistent with the observed behaviour; the reconciler did not re-fetch it. The SME's htmlFor-label-outside-the-form control (accepted) is critic-reported and the edu critic reports the same, not rerun. The reconciler's own inside-form aria-labelledby control was accepted with exit 0. Severity: low. The path needs markup the README does not ask for, and it fails closed with a wrong diagnosis, not a wrong verdict. This finding does not justify a fifth loop on its own; include it only if Firstmate authorizes one. Claim verified true. The module teaches a visible required marker: accessible-forms artifact.md says to show required fields in the visible label text, its example label reads 'Phone (required)', and its recap says to mark required fields in the visible text. README task 2 says only 'mark both required'. The starter TASK 2 comment narrows that to the required attribute but does not say the caption must stay exact. All public tests from task 2 on, and the Task 8 variant, find the name field by the exact text 'Service name'. Reproduced by the reconciler on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 044631bf with the private overlay copied over the starter, using the overlay's own reference learner test unless stated otherwise. With only the solved form's name label text changed to 'Service name (required)', the run shows 'Test Files 7 failed | 1 passed (8)' and 'Tests 7 failed | 1 passed (8)', each failure with 'Unable to find a label with the text of: Service name', exit 1. The oracle is never reached. Severity: low, but it is the closest of the loop-5 findings to substantive and is flagged to Firstmate as such. It is the only one that a learner reaches by following the module's own teaching rather than by changing markup beyond the README: a learner who reads 'mark both required' through the module's guidance can change the shipped caption text. It stays low because it fails loudly in the public suite on the first run after task 2, and every message names the exact caption the tests expect. The learner can recover in one edit, and the starter TASK 2 comment, read literally, points to the required attribute. It is not a false rejection by the Task 8 oracle, and it does not change what a correct learner who keeps the shipped captions sees. Fix direction: in README task 2, and in the starter TASK 2 comment if it is changed, say to mark both fields with the required attribute and to keep the label text exactly 'Service name' and 'Owning team', because the tests find the fields by that text. Optionally, the README could say that a visible required marker belongs outside the label text in this lab. Accepting a visible marker in the tests (regex or non-exact label queries in every public test and the variant) is a larger change and is not recommended. This is a README wording change; it does not touch the harness. This finding does not justify a fifth loop on its own; include it only if Firstmate authorizes one. Correction-loop status: this lab has already had four correction loops (89064f80, 30cd7583, 8543f338 and 044631bf, the last authorized by Firstmate under key react-forms-loop4-correction). Any byte-changing fix for this finding is a fifth correction loop and needs a new Firstmate decision. The author must not edit any lab byte for it until Firstmate makes that decision. Firstmate's condition for a fifth loop (a substantive medium or high finding remains) is not met by this finding.
